angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G), matched to the same NFL route families (slant, out, hitch, in, corner) and tested against season separation over expected on held-out draft classes; positive use = last-season SOE as a ranking for day-3 / undrafted receivers, benchmarked against a pick-and-routes forecast.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration magnitude (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill x Combine year, averaged over route drills and reliability-shrunk; same code on NFL snaps of the same route families
headline_number: One primary held-out estimate (average of plain and ridge no-tracking forecasts, both refitted in 2,000 class-stratified resamples): -0.8 in of season SOE per sd of Break G, 90% interval -2.8 to +1.3 (n=116); sceptical-prior posterior -0.7 [-2.6, +1.2], P(>= +3 in) = 0.1%. Last-season SOE carries 0.57 in per in beyond pick and routes [0.33, 0.73] (53 pairs, receiver-clustered); day-3/UDFA pool 0.45 [0.09, 0.90], but the yes/no rule ties a pick-and-routes ranking there (6/12 each, base 40%).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of the round-13 winner (round_13/cand_2, 8.45). Football: lede and action 1 now refer to the day-3/UDFA pool only and say the yes/no rule is directional (6/12 vs 2/8, base 40%, gap 25 [-14, 58]); all-rounds 62% vs 19% no longer quoted as the rule's result. New pick-and-routes baseline (forecast fitted on the other season pair, same list size): ties the SOE rule in day 3 (6/12), trails it by 12 pts [-7, 28] across all rounds; persistence net of that forecast 0.57 [0.33, 0.73], day 3 0.45 [0.09, 0.90]. Price reconciled: only the held-out 14% [5, 23] is quoted, and Figure 3B labels the diamond with that number. 2026 shortlist table (13 names, routes, SOE, Break G, soft cutters flagged as test cases); drill-vs-tape decision table with route-family coaching (Boutte, Smith, Bond, Bobo) and two historical cases (Washington kept by SOE despite soft cut and hit; Palmer hard cut + shortlisted and missed). Holm, Bonferroni, ledger and ridge detail removed. Data science: ridge vs plain collapsed into one primary (their average) with the ridge weight's interval (0.72 [-0.65, 1.69]); Bayesian sceptical-prior posterior; disattenuated drill-to-game correlation on 99 players with 8+ NFL breaks (r -0.05 [-0.21, 0.12], corrected -0.14 [-0.94, 0.48]); time-forward (2024->25) and backward shortlist scoring; receiver-clustered intervals throughout; Nacua-free YPRR kept in appendix. Writeup: one pool per number; 'The test' is a 6-row robustness table; YPRR, catch-over-expected, QB model and p values moved to the appendix; 'Why it matters' rewritten as motivation; metric paragraph uses the coach definition, no 'frozen and hashed'. 1,945 words by wc -w, 1,776 by check.py. Viz: Fig 1 now four players (2x2 pairs), readouts 12.5 pt, median path coloured by acceleration on one shared g scale, forecast-error strip replaced by a drill-vs-NFL Break G dumbbell in sd; Fig 2 (chain) cut to two panels with 8+ break players highlighted and the disattenuated estimate printed; Fig 3 = bootstrap + prior + posterior with the +3 in zone, and a decluttered price-vs-value panel with no secondary axis; Fig 4 shortlist with the pick-and-routes baseline rows, no label collisions, soft/hard counts in the note.
open_risks: Headline is still a bounded null for Break G; losses down to -2.8 in per sd are not excluded
The day-3/UDFA yes/no shortlist ties the pick-and-routes ranking (6/12 each); only the continuous persistence slope is firm there, on 20 pairs from 16 receivers
Disattenuated drill-to-game correlation has a very wide interval (-0.94 to 0.48) because NFL break reliability from 40 sampled plays is low (0.30)
Ridge forecast's held-out weight is unstable (0.72 [-0.65, 1.69]); the 'average of two forecasts' primary is itself a post hoc choice made after both versions were seen
Route-family coaching notes in the decision table rest on 3-14 sampled snaps per receiver
Game tracking is a 40-play sample per player, half selected for high EPA; the route-mix adjustment uses only the random half
